title: Soft Light
description: Soft light in soft light cinematography comes from a large apparent source and produces gradual shadow transitions and wrap around the face or body. Speculars get larger and dimmer; texture is reduced.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Kindness, memory, overcast, a north window: the key still has a side, but the nose shadow is a gradient. Skin holds, rooms feel breathable.
You can still have contrast if the fill is low; softness is not high-key. It is the wrong tool for a gobo of blinds, a noon duel, or a split that needs a knife edge.
If the source becomes so large it surrounds the subject, direction dies and you have ambient soup.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Make the last surface before the subject large: silk, book light, overcast sky, big window, bounce wall. Closer and larger is softer.
Color is often daylight 5600K through diffusion, or tungsten through a large shade. Keep a key side.
Prompt: Soft wrapping light on [Subject] from a large source, gentle shadow transitions, luminous skin, north-window daylight.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for beauty, memory, or kindness, a daylight interior, a close-up that should not cut pores into craters. Do not use it when you need projected pattern or interrogation.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Hard light is the opposite quality. Bounce light is a method of getting soft.
Window light is often large and soft by architecture. Glam uses soft keys plus diffusion and catchlights.
High-key lighting uses soft sources and a lot of fill; you can have soft low-key if the wrap is large but isolated.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: The Tree of Life and Call Me by Your Name let large daylight sources wrap skin and rooms. The softness is the size of sky and window, not a beauty filter named glow.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is hard light or directionless ambient. The tell is razor edges, or no key side at all.
Fix it by enlarging the source and keeping it on one side of the face.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is soft light in film?
Light from a large apparent source that wraps the subject and makes shadow edges gradual. Texture is reduced; direction can still exist.
Soft light vs bounce light
Soft describes the quality. Bounce is one way to create it, by reflecting off a large surface. A silk in line with the lamp is another way.
When should I use soft light?
Use it for kindness, memory, and most daylight interiors. Skip it when you need graphic shadow or a sharp gobo.
How do I prompt soft light for AI image or video?
Specify a large source, wrapping light, gentle shadow transitions. Name a window or silk on one side so direction remains.
